title: SIU says police officers who shot Aurora teen won't face charges
subtitle: Parents of Mikail Rashid are conducting their own investigation into the October death, which police say involved a false report of a break-and-enter.
article: Ontario's police watchdog says it will not lay charges against the officers who shot and killed a 17-year-old in Aurora during an "exchange of gunfire" outside his home in October.

Mikail Rashid was shot on Oct. 30 as York Regional Police responded to a call for a break-and-enter on Downey Circle, near Bayview Avenue and St. John's Side Road, according to the Special Investigations Unit, which probes deaths involving police.
He was pronounced dead at the scene.

In a report Thursday, SIU director Joseph Martino "found no reasonable grounds" to believe the officers committed a criminal offence when firing at Rashid. He alleged that he had made up the report of a break-and-enter so he could shoot and kill police officers.

"For whatever reason, it seems (Rashid) had set in motion a plan to lure police to his home where it appeared he intended to shoot and kill officers responding to a fake report of a break-and-enter in progress," Martino said in the report.
Rashid's parents said in a statement they were conducting their own investigation into his death - to "try to get to the bottom of what really happened."

"This SIU report does not describe the Mikail we knew. Mikail was a kind, loving, straight-A student, who literally refused to even hurt spiders," said the statement, shared with the Star through their lawyer, Nader Hasan.
"This report will not be his legacy."

The SIU said Rashid was trying to enter the side door of his home before the first officer on scene was hit in the face by a pellet. More police arrived shortly after and Rashid allegedly fired multiple shotgun rounds at the officers from about 15 to 30 metres away while he was also armed with a machete. All four officers fired shots.
"The officers' lives were in immediate peril and it was imperative that the Complainant be incapacitated as quickly as possible."

Martino concluded the officers were "duty-bound to attend to do what they reasonably could to enforce the law and ensure public safety," adding that "it was necessary to do so to protect themselves from a reasonably apprehended attack."
Rashid's mother, Lala Rukh, told the Star in October, "It does not make sense. "He would not break and enter into his own house. Why would he need to? He has the keys."
The report says "ten projectiles and a fragment" were removed from Rashid during his post-mortem examination.

Forensic investigators at the scene say they found two live shotgun shells, seven discharged shells, and one pump action shotgun that contained three live rounds as well as a total of 45 .223 shell cases, four 9-mm shell cases, one .22-calibre rifle and numerous .22 shell casings.
One officer sustained minor injuries in the shooting and was taken to hospital, the unit says.
